React shows a bordered Recent activity card with a fox icon and yellow status chip; Android removes the card and icon and places the yellow chip directly below the profile badges.
Android omits the View migration log link and adds a Report issue row to the action card.
The comparison bounds differ by 259 px: React is 390×1638 while Android is 390×1897, preventing one-to-one vertical alignment.
likelyCauses: Android uses stacked detail rows instead of React's two-column label/value layout.
The Android navigation configuration contains an extra Activity item.
The Android profile header uses a different recent-activity/status rendering structure.
The Android migration and action-menu component definitions differ from React.
The visual test used an element crop for React and a manually sized viewport for Android.
cases.suggestedOwner: Cross-platform profile screen owner, with Android UI and visual-test harness support
suggestedFixes: Render Info and Runtime config with matching two-column widths, row heights, gaps, and typography on both platforms.
Align the navigation tab set and order, and verify that the rightmost tab is clipped identically.
Restore the bordered Recent activity card and fox icon, and position the yellow state chip consistently with React.
Reconcile the migration controls and action list by restoring View migration log and removing or intentionally documenting Report issue.
Capture both platforms with the same screen-route crop contract and canonical 390×1638 bounds before comparing pixels.

summary: React shows a pale-peach error panel stating that the tab failed to load, with an outlined Retry button; Android replaces this with a populated raw-log view and omits both the error message and Retry action.
Android adds a rounded segmented control with a yellow, dark-outlined Raw Log selection and a gray Subagents 0 option; React has no corresponding control.

Android uses a vertical timeline with yellow and green square state indicators, gray monospaced descriptions, and right-aligned timestamps. React uses large black sans-serif error text with no timeline or state indicators.
The React capture is shorter and leaves a large blank white area below the error panel, while Android content continues through the full viewport.
likelyCauses: The platforms were captured in different Activity-tab states: React encountered a tab-load failure while Android successfully rendered raw activity data.
React and Android implement different Activity-content components rather than sharing the same state and layout contract.
Different full-page content heights or capture behavior produced the padded React canvas.
cases.suggestedOwner: Agent-detail Activity feature owner, with the React and Android implementers and the Slock capture pipeline owner
suggestedFixes: Align the Activity-tab state contract so both platforms render the same error panel and Retry action when loading fails.

If the raw-log view is intended on Android, port the segmented control, timeline markers, timestamps, and descriptions to React; otherwise remove the Android-only log view and show the equivalent error state.
Match typography by using the intended font family, type scale, and text colors for status labels, descriptions, and timestamps.
Align the main content's horizontal inset, top spacing, divider placement, corner radii, borders, and timeline component bounds.
Normalize capture height and eliminate blank padding before rerunning the Slock comparison.

summary: Section header titles differ in capitalization: React shows "Joint channels" and "Direct messages" (sentence case) while Android shows "Joint Channels" and "Direct Messages" (title case).

Android renders a gray "0" count badge next to every section header (Pinned, Joint Channels, Channels, Direct Messages); React shows the badge only on "Joint channels" and "Channels", omitting it on Pinned and Direct messages.
The Android "Joint Channels" header is missing the "+" (add) action button that React renders next to the sort arrows; Android shows "+" only on the Channels header.

Vertical rhythm differs: React leaves a large empty gap (~90dp) between the Pinned header and the Joint channels header, while Android's sections are packed more tightly, shifting Joint Channels, Channels, Direct Messages and their skeleton rows upward relative to React.

Typography weight/size mismatch: React's "Saved" title and section headers render heavier/larger than Android's, and the React bottom-nav "Home" label is bolder with a taller nav bar than the Android counterpart.
likelyCauses: Android hardcodes Title Case section titles instead of reusing the shared/i18n string resource used by React.
Android always renders the section count badge, while React renders it conditionally (only when a count is bound).
The add-channel action was omitted or conditionally gated in the Android Joint Channels header row.
Different spacing tokens between platforms (CSS rem/gap values vs Android dp margins) for collapsed section headers.
Typography token mapping differs (font family, weight and size) for the page title, section headers and bottom-nav labels.
cases.suggestedOwner: Android UI engineer / shared cross-platform design-system owner
suggestedFixes: Use one shared string resource for section titles so both platforms render "Joint channels" and "Direct messages" identically.
Align count-badge rules: render the badge on all section headers (including Pinned and Direct messages) in both platforms, or hide it everywhere, using the same badge size/offset from the label.
Add the "+" add button to the Android Joint Channels header, matching React's icon size, stroke weight and right-aligned position.
Normalize section spacing: use the same dp value for the gap below the Pinned header (and other section margins) in the Android theme as the React layout.
Match font tokens for the "Saved" title, section headers and the bottom-nav active "Home" label (weight, size, line height) and align the bottom navigation bar height/padding.
intentional: The yellow app-bar banner with the "Visual Server" dropdown and bell icon, and the five-item bottom tab bar with a yellow active Home pill, appear intentionally consistent across platforms.

summary: Android renders the timestamp as "unknown time" while React shows the formatted value "07/13 13:56".
Android truncates the preview one character earlier: "Keeps visual tes..." versus React's "Keeps visual testi...".
likelyCauses: Android is taking a missing-timestamp fallback path instead of formatting the available message timestamp.
The wider "unknown time" fallback reduces the space allocated to the adjacent preview in the metadata row.
cases.suggestedOwner: Android thread message-row and timestamp formatting team
suggestedFixes: Parse and format the Android timestamp as "07/13 13:56", matching the React value.
Reserve stable space for the timestamp or make preview width independent of the fallback text so the preview retains the same truncation point.
If the timestamp is genuinely unavailable, use the same fallback label and width as React.
intentional: Android renders full-width CJK punctuation at a full em width, which can alter spacing and line wrapping relative to Chrome; this is accepted platform behavior.

summary: The Android header shows the placeholder “unknown time,” while React displays the actual timestamp “07/13 19:25.”
likelyCauses: The Android message-header timestamp value is not being parsed, mapped, or formatted and falls back to the unknown-time label.
cases.suggestedOwner: Android message row/header timestamp rendering
suggestedFixes: Pass the source timestamp into the Android header and format it with the same locale and pattern as React: “07/13 19:25”.
Use “unknown time” only when the source timestamp is genuinely missing or invalid.
Add a regression case covering a valid message timestamp.
intentional: Spacing or wrapping around full-width CJK punctuation may differ because Chrome trims the punctuation while Compose renders it at a full em width; this is accepted platform behavior.

summary: Label casing differs: React shows 'Create agent' and 'Add computer', Android shows 'Create Agent' and 'Add Computer'.
Android dialog is positioned ~30dp higher in the viewport and is ~20-25dp taller than the React dialog (top edge ~260dp vs ~291dp, height ~252dp vs ~229dp).
Internal vertical spacing differs: the gap between the title row and the blue callout is much larger on Android (~32dp vs ~14dp), while the callout-to-footer gap is slightly tighter.
Callout body copy wraps at a different point (React breaks after 'runtimes on it,', Android after 'runtimes on') because the Android callout has ~18dp inner horizontal padding vs ~14dp in React.

Footer row alignment differs: Android's Cancel sits further left of the CTA, the primary button has ~30dp right padding vs ~20dp in React, the X close glyph is larger, and the callout blue plus CTA pink are slightly more saturated on Android.
likelyCauses: Android Compose dialog uses its own padding/typography scale instead of the shared web design tokens (dialog padding, header/callout gaps, footer spacing).
Different font stack and metrics (web font vs Roboto/system default) plus different callout inner padding, changing text line breaks.
String resources were written independently from the React copy, producing title-case differences in the header and CTA.
Android renders the dialog with a different vertical placement rule (offset/bottom-sheet-like anchoring) rather than the React dialog's centering offset.
Color tokens for the info callout and primary button were converted by hand rather than sourced from the shared palette.
cases.suggestedOwner: Android (Compose) UI / design-system team, paired with the React dialog owner
suggestedFixes: Match the React dialog's vertical placement and height: same top offset (~291dp) and same overall dialog height (~229dp), or reproduce the React centering rule exactly.
Align the Android callout's inner padding to the React value (~14dp horizontal) so the body text breaks after 'runtimes on it,'.
Match the internal vertical rhythm: header-to-callout gap ~14dp and callout-to-footer gap ~25dp as in React.
Normalize copy to the baseline strings ('Create agent', 'Add computer') in Android string resources, or update both platforms if title case is intended.
Reuse the shared tokens for the callout blue, primary pink, footer gap (Cancel-to-CTA) and CTA right padding (~20dp), and set the close X to the same size (~24dp) as React.
intentional: The ~30dp higher placement may be an intentional Android convention for bottom-anchored dialogs; confirm with design before changing, but the height and spacing deltas still need matching.

summary: Android shows an extra red status line under the header ("Update the app to save changes to this agent.") that is absent from the React panel.

Android is far denser vertically: the same field list renders in 1676px vs 1937px in React (~261px / 13% shorter), with tighter label-to-field and field-to-field gaps; the largest visible extra gap in React is between the "Switch, off" and "Switch, on" cards.
React's hint renders "link" as a styled hyperlink with a trailing external-link arrow (↗); Android renders the same hint as plain muted text with no arrow or link styling.

The key/value editor is structured differently: React uses compact side-by-side inputs separated by "=" with a gray trash-can delete icon and a "+ Add variable" button; Android stacks per-row "Key"/"Value" column headers, uses a red "×" remove glyph, labels the section "Key/value, empty (optional)" / "Key/value, filled (optional)", and the button reads "+ Add env var".

React's "URL, filled" input retains a red/error border while the same field on Android uses a neutral dark border; the crops also use different contracts (baseline element/component-bounds 390x1937 vs current manual viewport 390x1676), so the bottom regions are not aligned for comparison.
likelyCauses: Android build injects a platform-specific app-update/agent warning banner that has no React counterpart.
Divergent spacing tokens: Android Compose theme applies smaller vertical padding, label gaps, and section spacing than the React CSS.

Key/value row component was implemented independently per platform (equals-sign + trash icon in React vs labeled Key/Value columns + red × in Android) with inconsistent CTA copy ("Add variable" vs "Add env var").
Hint/link component differs: React appends an external-link icon and link styling; Android uses a plain text label.

Form validation styling diverges (error border persisting on the filled URL field in React), and the Slock crop contract mismatch (element vs manual viewport) makes the height difference partly a capture artifact.
cases.suggestedOwner: Android Runtime Form / Compose component owner, with the shared design-system (form tokens) owner for spacing and error-state parity
suggestedFixes: Remove or gate the "Update the app to save changes to this agent." banner so it does not appear in the Android screenshot, or add an equivalent (hidden) React element if the message is required.
Align Android's vertical padding, label spacing, and section gaps to the React layout (or update the React spacing tokens) so the form height matches the 1937px baseline within tolerance.

Rebuild the Android key/value editor to match React: side-by-side key/value inputs with an "=" separator, a gray trash-can delete affordance, and the "+ Add variable" label (drop the per-row Key/Value headers and red ×), or update React to the Android pattern if the new design is preferred.
Render the hint link on Android with the same link color/decoration and the trailing external-link (↗) icon used in React.

Fix the URL field error-border state so a valid filled URL uses the neutral border on both platforms, and re-run Slock with the same crop contract (element/component-bounds) on both sides so bottoms are comparable.
intentional: The differing crop modes (React element/component-bounds vs Android manual viewport) may be an intentional capture setup; the 1676px Android viewport can also truncate any content below "+ Add env var".
The "Update the app to save changes to this agent." message may be intentional platform-only agent guidance rather than a form defect.
